summary: Alfred von Gutschmid worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig (1848–1854) and studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen in 1851. He held professorships at Kiel, Königsberg, Jena, and Tübingen.

Alfredo Trombetti was a linguist who graduated from the University of Bologna around 1887–1891. He served as professor of Semitic philology (1904) and glottology (1912) at Bologna, and taught Francesco Ribezzo.
Ali Beth was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda around 1938–1943. He later taught J. A. B. van Buitenen.

Ali S. Asani specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard College (~1973–1977) and Harvard University (~1977–1984), where he became a professor around 1983. He also served on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.

Alice Harris is a linguist who studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Harvard University (~1970–1976). She held faculty posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2002) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

Alice Margaret Stevenson specialized in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Somerville College, Trinity College Dublin, and Oxford, also studying under Arthur Anthony Macdonell around 1899–1904.
Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang (attested 2005) and held a professorship at Boston University (attested 2013).

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago (2000–2009) under supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, among other teachers, and became an associate professor at York University in 2009.

Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, as well as teachers Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and Harvard University (~1993–2000), and became an associate professor at the University of California, Irvine around 2006.

Allan G. Grapard worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. at INALCO, he served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1985 and held an endowed Shinto studies chair (~1986–2007).

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held teaching posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), the University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).

Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who received a doctorate from the University of Oxford by 1983. He became professor of Asian languages and literatures at Pomona College in 1981 and taught Alison Denton Jones.

Allan Harrison Fry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Princeton (1928–1932) and the universities of Basel and Bonn (1935–1937), later teaching at Catholic University of America (1941), Fordham University, and The New School.

Allen W. Thrasher is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at the Library of Congress (~1985–2012) and had an affiliation with the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1994).
Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as associate professor of Hindi literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Alnis Dickson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson completed an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer worked in Indology and archaeology. After earning a Ph.D. at Würzburg under Julius Jolly and studying with Georg Bühler, he worked at St. Xavier's College, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Lucknow State Museum.

Alois Closs worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He earned two doctorates and habilitated at the University of Graz, studied at the University of Vienna, taught at Akademisches Gymnasium Graz, and was a librarian at Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek.

Alois Müller worked in linguistics and librarianship. He held posts at the Vienna University Library (~1867–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and served as director of Graz University Library in 1879.
